body.en: Depreciation is charged at a fixed rate on the book value (*written down value*) at the beginning of each year. Because the book value keeps falling, the amount of depreciation falls every year, and the asset never reaches zero. This method is accepted by the income tax authorities and suits assets like machinery whose repair costs rise with age.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A machine is bought for 1,00,000 rupees and depreciated at 10 percent p.a. by the WDV method. Find depreciation for three years and the book value at the end of year 3.
Year 1: 10 percent of 1,00,000 equals 10,000 rupees; book value 90,000.
Year 2: 10 percent of 90,000 equals 9,000 rupees; book value 81,000.
Year 3: 10 percent of 81,000 equals 8,100 rupees; book value 72,900.
So the answer is Depreciation 10,000, rupees 9,000, rupees 8,100 rupees; book value 72,900 rupees.
